messages.content: Find me a documentary about global warming.

function.name: retrieve_scientific_paper
function.description: Fetches the details of scientific research paper based on its topic. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

year.description: Year of publishing of the research paper. If not specified, fetches the most recent paper

author.description: Author of the research paper. If not specified, fetches the paper with most citations

message.content:
Here are a few highly‑recommended documentaries that focus on global warming and climate change.  They’re available on major streaming platforms and offer a mix of scientific insight, personal stories, and calls to action.

| Title | Year | Key Themes | Where to Watch |
|-------|------|------------|----------------|
| **An Inconvenient Truth** | 2006 | Former Vice‑President Al Gore’s presentation of the science of climate change, the impacts on ecosystems, and policy solutions. | Netflix (US & Canada), Amazon Prime Video (US), Hulu (US) |
| **The 11th Hour** | 2007 | Narrated by Leonardo DiCaprio, this film examines the environmental crisis, the role of human activity, and potential solutions. | Amazon Prime Video (US), Hulu (US), YouTube Movies |
| **Before the Flood** | 2016 | Leonardo DiCaprio travels the world to document the effects of climate change and discusses ways to mitigate it. | Netflix (US & Canada), Amazon Prime Video (US), Hulu (US) |
| **An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power** | 2017 | Al Gore’s follow‑up, focusing on the political and economic barriers to climate action and the progress made since the first film. | Netflix (US & Canada), Amazon Prime Video (US), Hulu (US) |
| **The Climate Reality Project: Climate Change – The Facts** | 2019 | A short, data‑driven documentary that explains the science behind climate change and its global impacts. | YouTube (free) |
| **The 11th Hour: The Climate Change Documentary** | 2007 | (Same as above – included for completeness) | Amazon Prime Video (US), Hulu (US), YouTube Movies |

### Quick Tips for Watching

- **Netflix**: Most of the above titles are available in the US and Canada. If you’re outside these regions, check the local Netflix catalog or use a VPN.
- **Amazon Prime Video**: Offers both free streaming (if you’re a Prime member) and pay‑per‑view options.
- **Hulu**: Good for U.S. viewers; some titles may require a subscription add‑on.
- **YouTube Movies**: Free for short documentaries like “The Climate Reality Project” or pay‑per‑view for longer films.
- **DVD/Blu‑ray**: If you prefer physical media, all of these films are available for purchase or rent on major retailers.

These documentaries provide a solid foundation for understanding the science, impacts, and solutions related to global warming. Enjoy watching—and feel empowered to take action!
